_comment: Tracked country pairs: nuclear-armed state(s) with strained relations or direct confrontation. Order within a pair does not matter. Add pairs here; the worker computes tension from GDELT. Each pair carries a basis and a one-sentence why; sensitive:true marks pairs whose inclusion is contestable. Being listed is not an accusation or a prediction.

pairs.label: United States – Russia
pairs.note: New START expired Feb 2026 with no replacement (SIPRI).
pairs.why: Both states hold nuclear weapons, and they hold the two largest arsenals (SIPRI).

pairs.label: Russia – Ukraine
pairs.note: Nuclear-armed state in a direct war.
pairs.why: Ukraine holds no nuclear weapons. The pair is listed only because a nuclear-armed state is in a direct war with it.

pairs.label: India – Pakistan
pairs.note: Both nuclear-armed; SIPRI 2026 cites the outbreak of conflict between them.

pairs.label: India – China
pairs.why: Both states hold nuclear weapons and share a disputed border.

pairs.label: North Korea – South Korea
pairs.why: South Korea holds no nuclear weapons. The pair is listed because a nuclear-armed state shares a divided border with it.

pairs.label: North Korea – Japan
pairs.why: Japan holds no nuclear weapons. The pair is listed because it lies within range of a nuclear-armed neighbour.

pairs.label: Israel – Iran
pairs.note: Israel is an undeclared nuclear state; Iran is a threshold state, not a nuclear-armed one.
pairs.why: Israel is an undeclared nuclear state. Iran holds no nuclear weapons; it is listed as a threshold state because its enrichment programme is under international scrutiny (IAEA).

pairs.label: United States – Iran
pairs.why: Iran holds no nuclear weapons; it is listed as a threshold state because its enrichment programme is under international scrutiny (IAEA).
